rules.name: BLAZING PRESENCE
rules.turn:
spirit-phase, (move P L), presence-of S P, spirit:special S blazing-presence, land L
  >move P L
  ^blaze-trigger S L P
  ~blaze S L
blaze S L, track-fire S F, ~deal-damage L F
blaze S L, track-fire S F, ge F 2, ~add-blight L
blaze S L, beasts-at B L, ~push S B L
#acc blaze-dahan-option : e
blaze-dahan S D / blaze-dahan-option push
blaze-dahan S D / blaze-dahan-option stay
blaze S L, at D L, piece:kind D dahan, ~blaze-dahan S D
blaze-dahan S D
  ?[rng] C
  !(blaze-dahan-option C)
  ~blaze-dahan-choice S D C
blaze-dahan-choice S D C, is C push, at D L, ~push S D L
blaze S L, presence-of S X, spirit:special S destructive-nature, { move X destroyed => }
rules.evidence: move w2 l3; blaze wildfire l3; deal-damage l3 2 -> destroy Explorer; add-blight l3; push wildfire Beasts l3 -> l2; per-Dahan push/stay choice
rules.notes: Four sentences map to four rules on the `blaze` episode. Needed BASE-EXT Damage/Health (point-by-point damage with per-piece @sum damage) and a 'Fire showing on tracks' fact. Not modeled: 'If you add multiple Presence into a land at the same time, only do the above effects once' -- each Presence move triggers separately; deduping needs an 'Action' identity Turn doesn't expose. Port to fresh-left ^ / #acc (2026-10-12): the trigger is anchored on each phase episode (one rule per phase; the snippet shows the Spirit phase) instead of a generic `^phase` window, which no longer overlaps the moves in the phase. Anchoring on `turn` instead was tried and is wrong: the blaze then runs concurrently with the later phases, so its Blight is invisible to them.
rules.text: Post-Setup, after your [Presence] is added/moved, in the land it goes to: For each [Fire] showing on your [Presence] Tracks, do 1 Damage. If 2 [Fire] or more are showing on your [Presence] Tracks, add 1 [Blight] . Push all [Beasts] and any number of [Dahan] . If you add multiple [Presence] into a land at the same time, only do the above effects once.

rules.name: DESTRUCTIVE NATURE
rules.turn:
blaze S L, presence-of S X, spirit:special S destructive-nature, { move X destroyed => }
use-power _ _, presence-of S X, spirit:special S destructive-nature, { move X destroyed => }
rules.evidence: Blight added by blaze in l3 destroys neither w1 nor w2; a later Ravage cascade into l3 (seed 1) does destroy w1, as it should
rules.notes: Exceptions whose contexts are the Spirit-effect episodes (blaze, use-power) drop `move X destroyed` for this Spirit's Presence; cascades are nested inside the add-blight that caused them, so '(This includes cascades.)' is free. The contexts must be enumerated (Powers, special rules...); 'Spirit effect' is not a first-class notion.
rules.text: [Blight] added due to Spirit effects ( Powers, Special Rules, Scenario-based Rituals, etc ) does not destroy your [Presence] . (This includes cascades.)

base_ext: Invader Health; per-piece damage (@sum of +hit facts) and a point-by-point deal-damage loop with destroy at Health; track-fire fact; per-phase triggers anchored on each phase episode.
language_issues: core.t has no Blight supply / loss condition, so once all lands have Blight, cascades recurse forever (status: gas); this spirit's extra Blight makes that likely. A Blight supply limit would itself need an 'instead' exception whose context starts when the supply runs out.
Damage persisted as `+hit` facts never clears at Time Passes; per-turn damage needs a turn key.
'At the same time' (one Action adding several Presence) has no handle: Turn has no notion of Action identity to dedupe triggers on.
